The correct grade alone does not prove the procedure was sound; the reusable check is to require same-attribute evidence and to verify that every cited rationale claim appears in an observed result.

Trigger: Before finalizing a yes/no chest-radiograph answer about subdiaphragmatic free air on a named side, especially when phrase grounding returns a positive-sounding phrase with a bounding box.

Verification action: Convert the bounding box location to patient side using the frontal-image convention—patient left is image right, and patient right is image left. Confirm the grounded box is beneath the diaphragm on the side asked about. If the phrase says free air is noted but the box is on the opposite patient side, do not treat it as evidence for the asked side. Require direct same-question evidence or visual evidence from the asked-side region. In this case, the grounding box was lower image-left (patient-right), so it did not support free air on the patient-left side; the direct expert answer “No” and absence of asked-side evidence support “No.” If options are displayed, also map the supported answer text back to the displayed choice and check that the letter and text agree.

Trigger: Before finalizing a yes/no chest-radiograph answer about a specific finding such as “Is a pneumothorax present in the left apex?”, after a direct same-question image tool and/or grounded report has already returned evidence.

Verification action: Check the direct current-image tool output for the exact object and attribute, then compare it with any same-finding statement in the grounded report and with the terminal answer’s polarity. In this case, chest_xray_expert answered “No” to “Is there a pneumothorax in the left apex?”, and maira2_grounded_report stated “There is no evidence of pneumothorax”; the terminal answer “No” matched both. If options are displayed, map the supported text back to the displayed option and confirm the letter and text agree. If the tool and report conflict, resolve the conflict or report uncertainty rather than asserting. Do not treat a correct grade alone as proof of the procedure, and do not rely on a bare visual-inspection claim unless the observation is actually available.

Trigger: When finalizing a yes/no chest-imaging answer about a specific lung finding, such as lung consolidation, after consulting a direct same-question expert-QA tool and a grounded radiology report.

Observable verification action: Re-read each cited observation and confirm it addresses the same object and attribute as the question. Use the direct same-question QA polarity as the primary answer, and use the grounded report only as support for that same attribute. For example, if chest_xray_expert answers “No” to “Is there consolidation in the lungs?” and maira2_grounded_report says “Lungs are clear” with no consolidation finding, the supported answer is “No,” but the rationale should not claim that both sources explicitly stated “no consolidation” unless both did. If options are present, map the supported answer text back to the displayed choice and verify that its letter and text agree; if no options are present, finalize the text answer. A correct reference match alone does not prove the rationale or any option mapping is correct.
